REGIS REPORT

13 March 2026

Following up from our piece earlier this week on the potential negative impact of the Iran war on the Philippines, we revise our 2026E macro forecasts as follows:

 

  • GDP growth down to 4.5% from 5.5%
  • Inflation (average) up to 4.0% from 5.0%
  • 10-yr BVAL (yrend) up to 6.0% from 5.5%

 

 

Near-term, we are most concerned about electricity prices in the coming months. Nationwide, 75% of the energy mix of the country’s electricity generation (not capacity) was either coal (57%) or natural gas (18%). This is more pronounced in Luzon, at 81%, given nat gas fuels 25% of the grid. The timing couldn’t get much worse, as the country enters its summer months. Historically, April/May/June are the highest consumption months of the year.

 

Consumers will likely be hit with sharply higher electricity prices… assuming there are no major disruptions in the nat gas supply that is…

 

 

+++

 

Coal-and-power firm Semirara (SCC PM) held its 4Q/FY25 briefing yesterday while Robinsons Land (RLC PM) issued a press statement on its FY25 results yesterday. RLC will hold its earnings call today, with at least three other firms also doing so (Ayala Corp (AC PM), Universal Robina (URC PM) and Converge ICT (CNVRG PM)).

 

  • Robinsons Land (RLC PM) (+) - Robinsons Land’s FY25 recurring profit grew 9% to P13.5bn, in line with consensus but ahead of REGIS forecast. The mall segment outperformed our expectations, largely thanks to margin expansion, while residential revenue recognition also exceeded our forecasts. However, demand for RLC’s residential projects remain weak, with sales of both its standalone and JV projects at mere fractions of the pre-COVID levels.  

 

  • Semirara (SCC PM) (-) - During yesterday’s briefing, management attributed the 4Q25 coal sales volume drop to low inventory and limited production of commercial grade coal.  Consequently, 4Q25 profits fell 20% YoY to P3.3bn and brought FY25 profit to P13bn (-34% YoY), underperforming Regis and Street estimates. On the bright side, things are looking up this year due to better coal prices and a new mine that produces higher quality coal. On the issue of the impending bid for a coal contract extension, management expressed confidence that it can submit a compelling bid and also confirmed that there were discussions with Meralco regarding a potential partnership.

PROPERTY
RLC FY25 recurring profit rises 9%, ahead of REGIS forecast
  • Robinsons Land’s FY25 recurring profit grew 9% to P13.5bn, in line with consensus but ahead of REGIS forecast
    • The mall segment outperformed our expectations, largely thanks to margin expansion
    • Residential revenue recognition also exceeded our forecasts
    • However, demand for RLC’s residential projects remain weak
  • Mall revenue and margins expand
    • 4Q25 mall revenue rose 7% YoY as occupancy increased 1ppt YoY (flat QoQ) to 94%. In FY25, mall revenue grew 10%. We estimate that same-mall revenue growth was 7% for the full year.
    • RLC’s 4Q25 mall EBIT margin also expanded 2.6ppt YoY to 40.5%. For the full year, it rose 1.6ppt to 41.5%
  • Reservation sales remain weak
    • Reservation sales of JV projects fell 52% QoQ and 63% YoY to P820mn, about 15% of the 2019 average
    • Reservation sales of standalone projects declined 73% YoY to P1.1bn. While this is a 30% QoQ improvement, it only represents 22% of the 2019 average
  • Office occupancy declines due to completion of new buildings
    • 4Q25 office occupancy declined 3ppt QoQ to 85%, due to the completion of 104k sqm of new office space, which expanded the portfolio by 13%.
    • Excluding the newly completed buildings, occupancy rose 2ppt QoQ to 90%
  • The company will host a briefing at 10AM
  • RLC offers 4.3% dividend yield and is trading at 64% discount to NAV, 0.5X FY26E P/B, and 5.9X FY26E P/E

 

 

 

BANKS
Asset quality mixed in Jan, but PD ratios up both MoM and YoY

Banks’ asset quality numbers were mixed in January 2026, as the MoM is clouded in part by write-offs done in December, and also by the seasonal MoM decline in loan balances. That said, the YoY numbers were pretty mixed too, with NPL ratios down, but PD ratios up. As always, we use ratios excluding interbank loans (IBL) and reverse repos (RRP), given the large and volatile nature of those accounts.

 

NPL ratio (ex-IBL/RRP) of 3.50% in January jumped 19bps MoM, but was down 7bps YoY. In nominal terms, NPLs stood at P24.7bn, up 4.7% MoM and up 7.4% YoY. However, Past Due (PD) ratio of 4.52% deteriorated both MoM (+27bps) and YoY (+11bps). The Peso value of PDs were up 5.6% MoM and 12.4% YoY. To the upside, Restructured Loans (RLs) stood at 2.14%, up just 2bps MoM and down 3bps YoY. NPL Cover slipped to 94.2%, down from 97.2% in December and from 95.3% in Jan 2025.

 

The NPL data were also all over the place by bank type. The worrying trend, though, is that PD ratios are sharply up, nearly across the board in January both on a MoM and YoY basis.

 

Meanwhile, loan growth (ex-IBL/RRP) slowed again to 9.73% YoY, a smidge slower than the 9.88% clocked in December 2025. LDRs, though, inched up to 73.3% from 72.6% at end-2025.

 

We will be watching both the loan growth and the PD data closely, particularly given the inflationary and GDP contractionary potential of the ongoing war in Iraq and the rest of the Middle East.
